Scottsdale to Sedona Private Transportation, and From Phoenix

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private transfer to Sedona as one chauffeured vehicle booked for the move — a door address in Phoenix or Scottsdale, one in Sedona, one way or with the ride back. Two shapes price it. The hourly charter is fully published: $145 an hour in the Executive Black Sprinter against its 4-hour minimum, $580 before 8% tax. A transfer is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and longer transfers are priced from the drive with the empty return included; Sedona is beyond the radius, so the published $295 is the basis the drive adds to. Call (623) 986-6339.

What is a private transfer from Phoenix or Scottsdale to Sedona?

One chauffeured vehicle booked for the journey itself: a door address in the Valley, a door address in Sedona, the same chauffeur the whole way, one way or with the ride back. The shortlist runs from 8 seats to 56, and its transfer basis opens at $295 in the Executive Black Sprinter. The word doing the work is "transfer": you are going somewhere and you want to arrive. What this page will not settle in advance is your exact routing: "Airport and point-to-point transfers are priced as a trip with no hourly minimum — flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and longer transfers priced from the drive with the empty return included. An hourly charter starts at four hours on every vehicle except the 56-passenger motorcoach, which starts at five. Each extra stop on a transfer is $50, and stops on an hourly charter cost nothing. Anything the online quote cannot price — an unusual route, a multi-vehicle movement, a vehicle we hold for request only — goes to the reservations desk and comes back as a written quote before any card is charged."

How is a private transfer to Sedona priced?

Two published shapes, from one rate card. The hourly charter is published in full: 4 hours at $145 an hour is $580 in the Executive Black Sprinter, before 8% tax. The transfer carries no hourly minimum, and past the flat radius its figure is read from the drive. Which shape fits depends on the day. A one-way drop, or a there-and-back with nothing in between, is a transfer. A move with the vehicle held between is the hourly product: you buy the chauffeur's time too. The grid publishes one transfer figure per vehicle rather than one per route: flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and priced from the drive beyond that, with the empty return included. Sedona is beyond it, so that figure is the basis: it covers the first 60 minutes of vehicle time, out and empty back, and each further half hour is added at the vehicle's rate, with the total shown in the checkout once both addresses are entered. The checkout opens hourly at the funnel's 4-hour default, and the reservations desk settles which price your booking in writing. These are the current published rates and minimums; request a current quote for your date.

Which vehicles does this page price, and what does each one cost?

8 executive units, from 8 seats to 56. Hourly rates run $145 to $325 against each vehicle's own minimum; the published transfer bases run $295 to $1,250, and each extra half hour of the drive runs $73 to $163. 2 of the 8 publish no bag cap. Read it as the executive shortlist, not the whole fleet. This route carries no curated pool, so the picker offers every listed vehicle that seats your party; the table is the subset with forward-facing seats and an aisle, and its cheapest row is what this page's "From" rate resolves to. Hourly total is the rate times the billable hours at that vehicle's minimum. Each extra half hour is that rate halved, the increment the checkout adds beyond the basis. Add 8% Arizona tax. Who books a Sedona transfer rather than a tour?

Four patterns cover most of it: a group landing at Sky Harbor and going straight north, a resort-to-resort move between the Valley and Sedona, a one-way drop with the return left open, and a wedding or retreat party arriving across a day, all on the same 8 vehicles. The arrival is the commonest: a party lands, collects its bags and does not want a second journey to organise. Resort-to-resort moves and one-way drops are the other steady shape: only one direction needs a vehicle. Wedding and retreat parties arrive in pieces, which makes it several movements on one reservation, quoted in writing. Service areas at the Valley end are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley.

Should you book one way or both legs?

Book both together and the return carries a 20% credit on the published bases: in the Executive Black Sprinter that is $295 out and $236 back, $531 for the pair, before the drive is added. Booked separately later, the way back is a second transfer with no credit. The credit exists only when both legs are bought at once, never afterwards. So the question is whether the return date and time are known. If they are, both legs is the cheaper shape; if not, book the leg you are sure of. Stops are charged on each leg, $50 at a time, so a return with a detour costs more than the paired basis above.

Is this a Sedona transfer or a Sedona day trip?

Both exist here and they are different products, so say plainly which you want. A transfer is this page: a move, priced as a trip or hourly, on 8 vehicles. A day trip keeps the vehicle and the chauffeur with you all day, and it is booked on the Sedona Red Rocks tour page instead. If the question is "get us there", book here. If it is "spend the day up there and bring us home", the tour page has the hours and the day-rate arithmetic. A wine day in the Verde Valley is a third page again. The practical test is whether anything waits. If the vehicle drops you and leaves, it is a transfer. If it sits while you walk, eat and come back, it is a chartered day priced by the hour.

What is included, and how do the deposit and cancellation work?

The vehicle, the chauffeur and the fuel, plus 8% Arizona tax and nothing else. A 50% deposit holds the booking and the balance is charged 48 hours before pickup. Cancel 14 or more days out and it refunds in full. The published inclusion list applies to any chauffeured booking. "A professional chauffeur on every vehicle, background- and MVR-checked" "A licensed and insured, locally owned operator" "Tax only — no booking fee, no service charge, no fuel surcharge, and gratuity never added for you" And: "Bottled water on board, the one complimentary amenity on every ride" Not included: checkout add-ons, hours past the window, and stops beyond pickup and drop-off on a transfer. Two house rules matter on a long private move: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." and "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Inside 14 days the deposit is kept and the rest refunded; inside 72 hours nothing is. A larger movement changes the tier, not the price: 20 or more passengers, or 2 or more vehicles, is a large group — full refund 30 or more days out, deposit kept to 14 days.

Things to know

  • Can I book one-way private transportation from Phoenix or Scottsdale to Sedona? — Yes. Choose One way in Trip preferences, enter the Phoenix or Scottsdale pickup and exact Sedona endpoint, and list every passenger and bag. The accepted pickup procedure, vehicle, route, service window, and price are confirmed in writing.
  • How do I request a Sedona round trip with a different return date? — Use the form's primary date and pickup time for the outbound trip, choose Round trip, and put the return date, requested return pickup time, Sedona address, and Phoenix or Scottsdale destination in the trip-notes field. The return is not accepted until both directions are confirmed in writing.
  • Can I keep the vehicle hourly for stops in Sedona? — Yes. Choose Hourly / multiple stops and enter the requested working service window and known stops. The website shows a vehicle-time estimate from the selected vehicle's published rate and minimum; route, wait time, parking, overtime, and date-specific costs are reviewed separately.
  • What arrival time should I enter for Sedona? — Enter the pickup time and desired arrival target, then include any fixed hotel, dining, activity, or check-in time in the notes. Arrival is a planning target, not a guarantee, because traffic, weather, road conditions, stops, and access can change the drive.
  • How much luggage fits on a Sedona transfer? — Cargo fit depends on the selected vehicle, passenger count, and size of every bag or piece of equipment. List full-size bags, carry-ons, child seats, mobility equipment, and other gear so practical vehicle fit can be confirmed before the reservation is accepted.
